title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is experiencing a mix of challenges and opportunities as missile production bottlenecks and budget increases vie for attention. Meanwhile, SpaceX's IPO and new collaborations signal a dynamic shift in market positioning.

themes.title: Missile Production Woes
themes.body: The push for increased missile production is stalling due to a shortage of solid rocket motors, highlighting the fragility of supply chains in defense. This bottleneck could have broader implications for military readiness if not addressed swiftly.

themes.title: SpaceX's IPO Surge
themes.body: SpaceX's shares surged nearly 20% following its historic IPO, making Elon Musk the world’s first trillionaire on paper. This financial windfall may reshape the competitive landscape, as other aerospace firms scramble to catch up.

themes.title: New Lunar Lander Plans
themes.body: Revised plans for the Artemis lunar lander are taking shape, reflecting ongoing adjustments in NASA's ambitious lunar ambitions. The changes may impact timelines and budgets, but they also signal a commitment to sustained lunar exploration.

themes.title: Defense Tech Investments
themes.body: The defense-tech sector is seeing renewed interest, with a $1.4B boost to space resilience in the FY27 budget. As companies pivot towards AI and satellite solutions, the landscape is ripe for innovation, albeit with a healthy dose of skepticism.
